subject: [PATCH v2 18/18] Documentation: iomap: update docs to reflect iomap_next model

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Reviewer Christoph Hellwig noted that passing the iterator in some form is a step forward, but suggested either passing it as a mutable object or as a const iterator along with non-const iomap and srcmap objects, referencing previous suggestions by Gao.
reviews.raw_body:
Well, at least passing the iter in some form.  Either just the iter
in mutable form, or a const iter plus non-const iomap and srcmap
as suggested by Gao and currently implemented for the next/iter
callback.

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested that instead of updating the documentation to reflect the new iomap_next model, it would be simpler and more maintainable to update the iomap_process helper to use the new signature and then switch over to it once, leaving the existing begin/end methods untouched.
reviews.raw_body:
It might make sense to simply use the new signature for the iomap_process
callbacks and switch over only once.  And never touch the existing
begin/end methods in the iomap_ops.

2026-07-06.patch_summary: This patch updates the iomap documentation to reflect the new iomap_next model, where every iomap operation takes a single iomap_next callback directly. The callback finishes the previous mapping and produces the next one. Most filesystems build it from begin and end helpers via the iomap_process helper. This change replaces the separate ->iomap_begin() and ->iomap_end() callbacks used in older versions of iomap.
